p.src: Baoyu, having let something slip and been left at a loss by Baochai's question, was trying to cover it up when Qiuwen came in and said, “Master is outside asking for Second Master.” Baoyu could not have wished for a better summons and left at once. When he reached Jia Zheng, Jia Zheng said, “I have summoned you for no other reason than this: since you are now in mourning and cannot attend school, you must review at home the essays you have studied. I happen to have some leisure these days, so every two or three days you are to write several essays for me to examine, that I may see whether you have made any progress lately.” Baoyu had no choice but to assent. Jia Zheng continued, “I have also told your brother Huan and your nephew Lan to go and review their lessons. If your essays are poor and you prove inferior even to them, that simply will not do.” Baoyu dared not speak. He answered “Yes” and remained standing where he was. “You may go,” said Jia Zheng. Baoyu withdrew and, on his way out, ran straight into Lai Da and several others coming in with a number of account books.

p.src: Baoyu flew back to his room. When Baochai learned that he had been summoned to write essays, she was rather pleased; Baoyu alone was unwilling, though he dared not neglect the task. Just as he was about to sit down and compose himself, two nuns entered. Baoyu recognized them as nuns from the Ksitigarbha Convent, and they greeted Baochai: “Our respects to Second Mistress.” Baochai replied with studied indifference, “Are you well?” Then she called to a servant, “Pour some tea for the reverend sisters.” Baoyu had meant to speak with the nuns, but seeing that Baochai appeared to dislike such people, he felt it improper to engage them in conversation. The nuns knew Baochai to be reserved, so they did not sit long and rose to take their leave. “Stay and sit a little longer,” said Baochai. One nun replied, “We have been performing rites at Iron Threshold Temple and have not called for quite some time to pay our respects to the ladies and mistresses. Now that we are here today, after seeing them we must also visit Fourth Miss.” Baochai nodded and let them go.

p.src: The nuns then went to Xichun's quarters. On seeing Caiping, one asked, “Where is your young mistress?” “Do not ask,” said Caiping. “For the past few days she has eaten nothing and has only lain there listlessly.” “Why is that?” asked the nun. “It is a long story,” said Caiping. “Once you see her, I expect she will tell you herself.” Xichun had already heard them and hurriedly sat up. “So you two are well, are you? “Once our family's fortunes declined, you stopped coming.” “Amitabha Buddha!” exclaimed the nun. “Whether rich or poor, a patron remains a patron. Besides, our convent belongs to your family, and we have received no end of kindness from the Old Lady. “Since the Old Lady's passing, we have seen all the ladies and mistresses except you. We were concerned about you, so today we came especially to visit you.” Xichun asked after the nuns of Water-Moon Convent. The nun replied, “There has been some trouble at their convent, and now the gatekeepers are reluctant to admit them very often.” Then she asked Xichun, “The other day we heard that Reverend Miaoyu of Green Lattice Convent had gone off with someone. What happened?” “What nonsense!” said Xichun. “Anyone who says such things had better beware of having their tongue cut out. “She was carried off by robbers; how can people still speak such vile slander?” The nun said, “Reverend Miaoyu was an eccentric woman. Perhaps all her piety was mere pretense. “Of course, it is hardly proper for us to say so before you. “She was nothing like coarse, simple folk such as us, who know only to recite sutras, invoke the Buddha, perform rites of repentance for others, and cultivate a blessed reward for ourselves.” Xichun asked, “And what do you mean by a blessed reward?” The nun replied, “A virtuous household such as yours need have no fear, but in other families even titled ladies and young mistresses cannot be assured of lifelong splendor. “When suffering and calamity descend, nothing can save them. “Only Guanyin Bodhisattva, in her great mercy and compassion, is moved to pity whenever people suffer and devises ways to deliver them. “That is why everyone speaks of Guanyin Bodhisattva, great in mercy and compassion, who rescues people from suffering and distress. “Though those of us who have taken religious vows endure far greater hardships than ladies and young mistresses, we are at least spared peril and calamity. “Even if we cannot become Buddhas or patriarchs, through cultivation we may be reborn as men in the next life, and that alone would better our lot. “It would be better than being born, as we are now, into a woman's body, unable even to voice all our grievances and vexations. “You may not know it, Miss, but once a young lady marries and must follow a husband, she is even more helpless for the rest of her life. “If one speaks of religious cultivation, the only thing that matters is practicing it sincerely. “Reverend Miaoyu believed her talents superior to ours and despised us as vulgar, never realizing that it is precisely the vulgar who can obtain blessed affinities.

p.src: “And in the end she has now met with a great calamity.” The nun's words struck such a chord with Xichun that she leaned forward over the table. Heedless of the maids' presence, she recounted how You-shi had treated her and all that had happened when she had recently been left to mind the house. Pointing out her hair for the nun to see, she said, “Do you take me for some irresolute creature clinging to a pit of fire? “I have long cherished this intention; I simply could not find a way to carry it out.” On hearing this, the nun feigned alarm. “Miss, you must never speak so! “If Mistress Zhen heard of it, she would curse us to death and drive us from the convent! “With your character and family standing, you will one day be matched with a fine husband and enjoy wealth and honor all your life.” Before she could finish, Xichun flushed and said, “If Mistress Zhen can drive you away, do you suppose I cannot?” Realizing that Xichun was in earnest, the nun decided to provoke her further. “Do not blame us for speaking out of turn, Miss, but how could the ladies and mistresses possibly indulge your wishes? “It would be unfortunate if the affair ended in an embarrassing uproar. “We say this only for your own sake.” “We shall see about that,” said Xichun. Caiping and the other maids, disliking the turn the conversation had taken, signaled to the nun with their eyes that she should leave. The nun understood. Already fearful herself and not daring to provoke Xichun any further, she took her leave and went out. Xichun made no attempt to detain her and merely sneered, “Do you imagine that your Ksitigarbha Convent is the only convent under heaven?” The nun dared not answer and went away.

p.src: Caiping saw that matters were taking a bad turn and, fearing that she might be held responsible, secretly went to tell Madam You, “The Fourth Young Lady still has not given up the idea of cutting off her hair. She has not been ill these past few days; she has simply been railing against her fate. Madam, please be on your guard. If anything should happen, the blame will fall upon us.” Madam You replied, “She does not truly want to become a nun. She is deliberately making trouble for me because the master is away from home. We can only let her have her way.” Caiping and the others could do nothing but continue trying to reason with her. Little did they know that Xichun would eat less with each passing day and think of nothing but cutting off her hair. Unable to bear the responsibility any longer, Caiping and the others had no choice but to report it everywhere they could. Madam Xing, Madam Wang, and the others also tried several times to dissuade her, but Xichun stubbornly refused to see reason.

p.src: Just as Madams Xing and Wang were about to tell Jia Zheng, word came in from outside: “Madam Zhen has arrived with the Baoyu of her family.” Everyone hurried out to receive them, and they sat down in Madam Wang’s apartments. They exchanged greetings and inquiries after one another’s health, which need not be related in detail. It need only be said that Madam Wang remarked that Zhen Baoyu was exactly like her own Baoyu and asked to see him. A message was sent out, and the servant returned to report, “Young Master Zhen is speaking with the master in the outer study. They have found one another so congenial that the master has sent for our Second and Third Young Masters, as well as young Master Lan, to dine outside. They will come in after the meal.” As soon as this was said, the meal was served inside as well. No more need be said of this.

p.src: Now Jia Zheng found that Zhen Baoyu’s appearance was indeed identical to Baoyu’s. When he tested the young man’s literary learning, Zhen Baoyu answered every question with perfect fluency, inspiring great respect in him. He therefore summoned Baoyu and the other two young men to admonish and encourage them by Zhen Baoyu’s example. Besides, he wished at last to bring Baoyu out and compare the two. Obeying the summons, Baoyu put on mourning clothes and came out with his brother and nephew. The moment he saw Zhen Baoyu, it seemed as though they were old acquaintances. Zhen Baoyu likewise felt that he had seen him somewhere before. The two exchanged salutations, after which Jia Huan and Jia Lan were presented to him. Jia Zheng had originally been sitting on the floor and had wished Zhen Baoyu to take a chair. But as a junior, Zhen Baoyu dared not take the seat of honor and instead had a cushion spread on the floor and sat upon it. Now that Baoyu and the others had come out, they could not sit beside Jia Zheng; yet since Zhen Baoyu belonged to a still younger generation, it would also have been improper to leave Baoyu and the others standing. Realizing the awkwardness, Jia Zheng rose, spoke a few more words, and ordered the meal to be served. “You must excuse me,” he said. “I shall leave the young fellows to keep you company. Talk freely together, so that they may profit from your excellent instruction.” Zhen Baoyu modestly replied, “Please do as you wish, honored uncle. It is I who was hoping to receive instruction from my honored cousins.” After exchanging a few more courtesies, Jia Zheng went away to the inner study. Zhen Baoyu made to accompany him out, but Jia Zheng stopped him. Baoyu and the others hastened a step ahead across the threshold of the study and stood watching until Jia Zheng had gone inside. Then they returned and invited Zhen Baoyu to sit down. They exchanged the customary courtesies for a while, speaking of their long admiration and earnest desire to meet; these need not be related in detail.

p.src: Now when Jia Baoyu saw Zhen Baoyu, he recalled the scenes in his dream. Moreover, he had long understood that Zhen Baoyu must be of one mind with him, and believed that at last he had found a kindred spirit. But since this was their first meeting, he could not presume upon him. And with Jia Huan and Jia Lan present, he could only praise him to the utmost: “I have long admired your distinguished name but have never had the opportunity of receiving your instruction in person. Meeting you today, I find you truly a man of the same order as an exiled immortal.” Zhen Baoyu had also long known Jia Baoyu’s character, and upon meeting him today found that the reports were indeed accurate. He thought, “He may study with me, but he cannot yet walk the Way with me. Since he bears the same name and appearance as I, he too must be an old spirit from the Stone of Three Incarnations. Since I have gained some slight understanding of principle, how could I refrain from explaining it to him? Yet this is our first meeting, and I do not know whether his heart is truly the same as mine. I had best proceed gradually.” He therefore said, “I have long known of your literary fame, honored cousin. You are the purest and most refined man to be chosen from among tens of thousands, while I am merely a dull, commonplace fool. I feel that my unworthy sharing of your name can only sully those two characters.” Hearing this, Jia Baoyu thought, “This man’s heart is indeed exactly like mine. But you and I are both men and cannot compare in purity with those girls. Why, then, has he begun treating me as though I were one of them?” He replied, “Your praise is far too generous, honored cousin; I truly do not deserve it. I am the coarsest and most foolish of men, nothing more than a stubborn stone. How could I compare with your lofty character and reputation, which make you truly worthy of the name we share?” Zhen Baoyu said, “When I was young, I did not know my own measure and fancied that I might still be cut and polished into something worthwhile. Little did I expect my family to decline. Over the past several years I have become more broken and worthless even than shards of tile and rubble. Though I would not presume to say that I have tasted every sweetness and bitterness, I have nevertheless gained some small understanding of the ways of the world and the feelings of men. You, honored cousin, have been raised in brocade and fed on delicacies, with every wish fulfilled. Your mastery of letters and statecraft must therefore surpass that of ordinary men; hence your honored father cherishes you and intends you to become a precious vessel of the court. That is why I said just now that you alone are worthy of your honored name.” Jia Baoyu heard that this line of talk was again approaching the old cant of those careerist drones and was considering how to answer. Jia Huan, meanwhile, had already grown displeased that Zhen Baoyu had not spoken to him. Jia Lan, however, found these words very much to his liking and said, “What you say, uncle, is certainly far too modest. When it comes to letters and statecraft, only what is gained through experience can be called true talent and genuine learning. I am still young and do not know what literature truly is, but when I reflect carefully upon what I have read, I find that a fine reputation and widespread renown are worth a hundred times more than rich food and embroidered garments.” Before Zhen Baoyu could reply, Jia Baoyu, increasingly displeased by Lan’s words, thought, “Since when did this child learn to spout such pedantic nonsense?” He therefore said, “I have heard that you too, honored cousin, utterly despise vulgar conventions and possess distinctive insights of your own into human nature and feeling.

p.src: “Today I have had the good fortune to meet you, a man of distinguished bearing, and hoped to receive instruction from you in truths that transcend the common and lead to sagehood, so that I might cleanse my worldly heart and open my eyes anew. I did not expect you to take me for a fool and answer me only with talk of worldly affairs.” Hearing this, Zhen Baoyu understood inwardly, “He knows what I was like in my youth, and so suspects that I am being insincere. I may as well explain myself plainly; perhaps he may yet become an intimate friend who truly understands me.” He therefore said, “Your lofty observations are indeed sincere and to the point. Yet in my youth I too deeply detested those stale conventions and worn-out sayings. But as I grew older year by year, my father retired from office and, being disinclined to receive callers at home, entrusted their reception to me. Later I met many eminent gentlemen, all men who brought distinction to their families and made names for themselves. Even when they wrote books and propounded doctrines, they spoke invariably of loyalty and filial devotion. Only by accomplishing something through moral conduct and enduring words can a man avoid having lived in vain in an age ruled by an enlightened sovereign, or failing to repay the care and instruction of his father and teachers. Thus I gradually cast off some of the foolish notions and infatuated sentiments of my youth. Even now I wish to seek teachers and friends who may instruct me in my ignorance. Having had the good fortune to meet you, I am certain you will have much to teach me. What I said just now was no empty courtesy.” The more Jia Baoyu listened, the more impatient he became; yet, unwilling to treat his guest coldly, he could only answer evasively. Fortunately, a message came from the inner apartments: “If the gentlemen outside have finished their meal, please ask Young Master Zhen to come inside and sit with us.” On hearing this, Baoyu seized the opportunity to invite Zhen Baoyu inside.

The more Jia Baoyu listened, the more impatient he became; yet, unwilling to treat his guest coldly, he could only answer evasively.
Fortunately, a message came from the inner apartments: “If the gentlemen outside have finished their meal, please ask Young Master Zhen to come inside and sit with us.”
On hearing this, Baoyu seized the opportunity to invite Zhen Baoyu inside.

p.src: Zhen Baoyu obeyed and went ahead, accompanied by Jia Baoyu and the others, to pay his respects to Lady Wang. Seeing Lady Zhen seated in the place of honor, Jia Baoyu first paid his respects to her, and Jia Huan and Jia Lan also came forward to greet her. Zhen Baoyu likewise paid his respects to Lady Wang. The two mothers and their two sons exchanged introductions and recognized one another. Although Jia Baoyu was already married, Lady Zhen was elderly and a longstanding relation; and when she saw that his features and build were exactly like her son's, she could not help becoming affectionate toward him. Lady Wang was still more delighted. Taking Zhen Baoyu by the hand, she questioned him about everything and thought him somewhat steadier and more mature than her own Baoyu. Looking again at Jia Lan, she found him remarkably delicate and handsome; though he could not equal the appearance of the two Baoyus, he was not far behind them. Only Jia Huan was coarse and clumsy, so a certain partiality inevitably showed in her manner. When everyone saw the two Baoyus together, they all came to look and exclaimed, “This is truly extraordinary! It would be remarkable enough for their names to be the same, but how can their faces and figures be identical as well? Fortunately our Baoyu is dressed in mourning; if they wore the same clothes, we could never tell them apart at a glance.” Among them, Zijuan was suddenly seized by a foolish fancy and thought of Daiyu. She said inwardly, “What a pity Miss Lin died! Had she lived and been matched with Zhen Baoyu, I daresay she might have been willing.” While she was thinking this, she heard Lady Zhen say, “The other day, when our master returned, he told me that our Baoyu is now of marriageable age and asked the master of this house to keep an eye out for a suitable match.” Lady Wang had already taken a great liking to Zhen Baoyu and replied readily, “I too should like to act as matchmaker for your son. There were four young ladies in our family. Of three there is no need to speak—some have died and others have married. There remains the younger sister of my eldest nephew Zhen, but she is several years too young and may not be a suitable match. But my elder daughter-in-law has two cousins, both handsome and accomplished. The second has already been betrothed, while the third would make an excellent match for your son. One of these days I shall propose the match on your son's behalf, though her family's circumstances are somewhat reduced at present.” Lady Zhen replied, “Madam, you are being too ceremonious again. What have we ourselves left nowadays? I only fear that others may despise us for our poverty.” Lady Wang said, “Your household has now received another official appointment. In time, not only will its former prosperity be restored, but it will surely flourish even more greatly than before.” Lady Zhen said with a smile, “I can only hope your words come true. If so, I must ask you to act as our matchmaker.” When Zhen Baoyu heard them discussing his marriage, he took his leave and withdrew. Jia Baoyu and the others had no choice but to accompany him to the study, where they found Jia Zheng already waiting; they remained standing and conversed for a few more moments. Then a servant from the Zhen household came to report to Zhen Baoyu, “Her ladyship is about to leave. Please return with her, young master.”

p.src: Now, ever since Baoyu had met Zhen Baoyu's father and learned that Zhen Baoyu was coming to the capital, he had looked forward to the meeting morning and evening. When they met that day, he had expected to find a kindred spirit; but after half a day's conversation, he discovered that they were as incompatible as ice and charcoal. He returned gloomily to his room, neither speaking nor smiling, but merely staring blankly. Baochai asked, “Does that Zhen Baoyu really look like you?” Baoyu replied, “His face does indeed look the same. But judging from his conversation, he understands nothing at all. He is merely another career worm.” Baochai said, “There you go slandering people again. What makes you think he is another career worm?” Baoyu replied, “He talked for ages without saying a word about illuminating the mind and seeing one's true nature. All he spoke of was scholarship and statecraft, and loyalty and filial devotion. If a man like that is not a career worm, what is he? It is only a pity that he was born with such a face. Now that he exists, I feel I no longer want even this face of mine.” Seeing him talk foolishly again, Baochai said, “You really do say the most laughable things. How can you possibly discard your own face? Besides, what he said is perfectly reasonable. A man ought by rights to establish himself and win a name. Who else is like you, forever absorbed in tender feelings and private affections? Instead of admitting that you yourself lack manly resolution, you call him a career worm.” Baoyu had already found Zhen Baoyu's words intolerable, and after this sharp rebuke from Baochai he grew still more unhappy. Sunk in a gloomy daze, he unwittingly brought on a recurrence of his old illness. He said nothing and merely grinned foolishly. Baochai did not understand and merely thought, “My words must have offended him, and that is why he is sneering.” So she paid him no further attention. Little did she know that he had already become somewhat deranged that very day; even when Xiren and the others tried to provoke him into speaking, he remained silent. After a night had passed, he rose the next morning still staring vacantly, showing every sign of his former illness.

p.src: One day, since Xichun remained determined to cut off her hair and become a nun, Madam You found herself unable to stop her. From Xichun's manner, it seemed that unless they consented, she was certain to take her own life. Though someone watched her day and night, this could not go on indefinitely, so Madam You told Jia Zheng. Jia Zheng sighed and stamped his foot, saying only, “Who knows what has been going on in the Eastern Mansion to bring matters to such a pass?” He summoned Jia Rong, gave him a stern lecture, and told him to speak to his mother and have her reason earnestly with Xichun. “If she insists on doing this, she is no daughter of our family.” Yet while Madam You might better have left her alone, the moment she tried to persuade her, Xichun became still more intent on dying. “A girl cannot remain at home all her life,” she said. “If I were to end up like Second Sister, the masters and mistresses would only be burdened with worry—and besides, she died in the end. Now, just regard me as already dead and let me enter religious life. Allowing me to pass my whole life in purity would be the truest kindness you could show me. Besides, I shall not even leave the estate. Green Lattice Nunnery stands on our own family's land, and I shall cultivate the religious life there. If I should need anything, you will still be able to look after me. The nun who took charge after Miaoyu is there now. If you grant my wish, I shall count my life as saved; but if you refuse, there is nothing else I can do—I can only die and put an end to it all. If I am allowed to fulfill my own wish, then when Elder Brother returns, I shall tell him myself that none of you forced me into it. But if I die, when Elder Brother comes home he may well say that you gave me no place here.” Madam You had never been on good terms with Xichun, and what the girl said seemed reasonable enough; she therefore had no choice but to report it to Lady Wang.

p.src: Lady Wang had already gone to Baochai's quarters. Seeing Baoyu distracted and beside himself, she grew anxious and rebuked Xiren: “You have all been far too careless. Why did no one tell me that Second Master was ill?” Xiren replied, “Second Master's illness has always come and gone; sometimes he is well, and sometimes he is not. He has gone every day as usual to pay his respects to you and has seemed perfectly well. It was only today that he became somewhat confused. Second Mistress was just about to report it to you, but she feared you might accuse us of making a fuss over nothing.” Hearing Lady Wang scold them, Baoyu's mind cleared for a moment. Afraid they would be unfairly blamed, he said, “Please do not worry, Mother. There is nothing seriously wrong with me; I merely feel a little oppressed at heart.” Lady Wang said, “You have always been prone to this illness. If you had told me sooner, we could have summoned a physician; would it not have been better to take a couple of doses of medicine and recover? If it grows as serious as it did when you lost the jade before, we shall have no end of trouble.” Baoyu replied, “If you are uneasy, Mother, have someone come and examine me, and I will take the medicine.” Lady Wang at once sent a maid out with instructions to summon a physician. With all her thoughts fixed on Baoyu, she forgot entirely about Xichun. After a while the physician arrived, examined Baoyu, and prescribed medicine, which he took. Lady Wang then returned to her own quarters.

p.src: After several days, Baoyu grew still more confused and even stopped eating, causing everyone to become alarmed. The household was also busy preparing to put off mourning, and there was no one free, so Jia Yun was summoned to attend to the physician. Jia Lian had no one available in his own household, so Wang Ren was invited to help manage affairs outside. Qiaojie, who wept for her mother day and night, also fell ill. Thus the Rong Mansion was once again thrown into utter turmoil.

p.src: One day, after returning home from the mourning observances, Lady Wang went personally to see Baoyu again. Finding him unconscious, everyone was so frantic that they did not know what to do. Weeping, Lady Wang told Jia Zheng, “The physician has given up the case and refuses to prescribe any more medicine. We can only prepare for the worst.” Jia Zheng sighed repeatedly. He had no choice but to go and see Baoyu himself; finding that his condition was indeed grave, he again ordered Jia Lian to make the necessary arrangements. Jia Lian dared not disobey and could only order the servants to begin preparations. He was short of money and wondering what to do when a man came running in and cried, “Second Master, disaster! More trouble has come upon us!” Jia Lian had no idea what had happened. Thoroughly alarmed, he stared and demanded, “What is it?” The page replied, “A monk has appeared at the gate holding the piece of jade that Second Master Baoyu lost. He says he wants ten thousand taels as a reward.” Jia Lian spat contemptuously in his face. “I wondered what calamity had occurred to make you panic like this! Have you forgotten the false jade that appeared last time? Even if it is genuine, the man is dying now—what use is the jade to him?” The page said, “I told him the same, but the monk said that if we gave him the silver, Second Master would recover.” Then a shout was heard from outside: “This monk is running wild! He has forced his way in, and no one can stop him!” Jia Lian said, “How can such an outrageous thing be allowed? Why do you not drive him out at once?” As the commotion continued, Jia Zheng heard what was happening and found himself at a loss as well. Just then someone came out from the inner rooms, weeping and crying, “Second Master Bao is failing!” Jia Zheng grew more anxious than ever. The monk was heard shouting, “If you want his life saved, bring me the silver!” Jia Zheng suddenly remembered that a monk had cured Baoyu's illness before. Now that another monk had arrived, perhaps he might prove their savior. But if the jade should prove genuine, what were they to do when the monk demanded his silver? After considering the matter, he decided to set that question aside for the moment; if Baoyu truly recovered, they could discuss it afterward.

p.src: Jia Zheng sent someone to invite him in, but the monk had already entered. Without bowing or saying a word, he ran straight toward the inner apartments. Jia Lian caught hold of him and cried, “The inner rooms are full of womenfolk! What are you, you wild creature, doing barging in there?” “If I am late,” said the monk, “he cannot be saved.” In his agitation, Jia Lian followed him, shouting wildly as he went, “Everyone inside, stop crying! A monk is coming in!” Lady Wang and the others were wholly absorbed in their weeping and paid no attention. Jia Lian came nearer and shouted again. Lady Wang and the others turned around and, seeing a tall monk, started in fright, with no time to withdraw. The monk walked straight to Baoyu’s kang. Baochai moved aside, while Xiren, seeing Lady Wang still there, dared not leave. Then the monk said, “Good patrons, I have come to return the jade.” As he spoke, he held up the jade and said, “Quickly bring out the silver, so that I may save him.” Lady Wang and the others were too distraught to judge whether this was true or false. “If you can restore him to life,” they said, “we shall have the silver.” The monk smiled. “Bring it, then.” “Do not worry,” said Lady Wang. “One way or another, we can turn our possessions into money.” The monk burst into loud laughter. Holding the jade beside Baoyu’s ear, he called, “Baoyu! Baoyu! Your precious jade has returned!” The moment he had spoken, Lady Wang and the others saw Baoyu open his eyes. “He is better!” cried Xiren. Baoyu immediately asked, “Where is it?” The monk placed the jade in his hand. At first Baoyu clutched it tightly; then, slowly regaining control of his hand, he held it before his eyes and examined it closely. “Ah,” he said, “it has been a long time!” Everyone inside and outside joyfully invoked the Buddha’s name; even Baochai forgot that a monk was present. Jia Lian also came over to look. Seeing that Baoyu had indeed revived, he rejoiced inwardly and hurriedly slipped out.

p.src: Without saying a word, the monk hurried after Jia Lian, seized him, and ran off with him. Jia Lian had no choice but to follow him to the front apartments, where he hastened to tell Jia Zheng what had happened. Delighted by the news, Jia Zheng immediately sought out the monk, bowed to him, and thanked him with a kowtow. The monk returned his bow and sat down. Jia Lian thought suspiciously, “He will surely refuse to leave until he has the silver.” Jia Zheng looked closely at the monk and saw that he was not the one he had met before. He asked, “Where is your honored monastery? What is your reverend name? Where did you obtain this jade? And how is it that my son revived as soon as he saw it?” The monk smiled faintly. “I do not know either. Just bring me ten thousand taels of silver, and that will settle everything.” Jia Zheng found the monk uncouth, but dared not offend him. “We have it,” he replied. “If you have it, bring it quickly,” said the monk. “I must be going.” “Please sit a little longer,” said Jia Zheng, “while I go inside and have a look.” “Go, then,” said the monk, “but be sure to return quickly.”

p.src: Jia Zheng did indeed go inside. Without stopping to announce himself, he went straight to Baoyu’s kang. When Baoyu saw that his father had come, he tried to rise, but he was too weak to get up. Lady Wang held him down. “Do not move,” she said. Smiling, Baoyu held up the jade for Jia Zheng to see. “My precious jade has come back,” he said. Jia Zheng gave it a cursory glance and realized that there was some deeper cause behind the matter. Without examining it more closely, he said to Lady Wang, “Baoyu is recovering. What shall we do about the reward money?” “Let us sell everything I possess if need be and give him the proceeds,” said Lady Wang. “I fear this monk does not really want silver,” said Baoyu. Jia Zheng nodded. “He seems strange to me as well, but he keeps insisting on silver.” “Go back out, sir,” said Lady Wang, “and keep him here hospitably for the time being. We can decide what to do afterward.” After Jia Zheng went out, Baoyu complained of hunger. He drank a bowl of congee and then asked for rice. The old serving-women duly brought some rice, but Lady Wang still dared not let him eat it. “It will do me no harm,” said Baoyu. “I am well now.” He leaned forward and ate a bowlful. His vigor gradually returned in earnest, and he asked to sit up. Sheyue stepped forward and gently helped him up. u.src: Jia Zheng did indeed go inside. Without stopping to announce himself, he went straight to Baoyu’s kang.
When Baoyu saw that his father had come, he tried to rise, but he was too weak to get up.
Lady Wang held him down. “Do not move,” she said.
Smiling, Baoyu held up the jade for Jia Zheng to see. “My precious jade has come back,” he said.
Jia Zheng gave it a cursory glance and realized that there was some deeper cause behind the matter. Without examining it more closely, he said to Lady Wang, “Baoyu is recovering.
What shall we do about the reward money?”
“Let us sell everything I possess if need be and give him the proceeds,” said Lady Wang.
“I fear this monk does not really want silver,” said Baoyu.
Jia Zheng nodded. “He seems strange to me as well, but he keeps insisting on silver.”
“Go back out, sir,” said Lady Wang, “and keep him here hospitably for the time being. We can decide what to do afterward.”
After Jia Zheng went out, Baoyu complained of hunger. He drank a bowl of congee and then asked for rice.
